verdict.strongest_transmitted_behavior: The board most strongly transmits the operational safety story: partial publication is never served, inconsistent writes are repaired or rolled back, live queries stay on the current index generation until a complete and consistent replacement can be atomically promoted, and the prior generation remains available for rollback.
verdict.most_consequential_loss: The most consequential loss is the detailed document-version lifecycle: the new/changed/unchanged hash branches, unchanged-content bypass, changed-version supersession, and deletion of stale derived records are not recoverable. In addition, the published stores are not explicitly connected to query retrieval, so a key serving relationship still requires inference.
verdict.overall_summary: The reconstruction communicates the RAG domain, major components, primary ingestion sequence, permission-aware hybrid retrieval, grounded-answer versus abstention branch, principal failure destinations, feedback loop, and index-generation rollout policy. It is usable for architecture discussion, but not yet an implementation plan: several system-defining versioning branches and cleanup rules are absent; per-fragment metadata invariants are softened; publication writes and their all-three consistency gate are only partially connected; and the serving path from published indexes into retrieval is implicit. There are no material contradictions or unsupported reconstruction claims.
